warm.li: I'd still love to teach {OTHER_nameDef}, whenever an evening comes free.

blunt.li: {OTHER_nameDef} needs a teacher, and I'm standing right here.

cold.li: Every week without lessons, {OTHER_nameDef} learns {SUBJECT} slower than {OTHER_pronoun} could.

warm.li: If {OTHER_nameDef} ever comes and asks, I'll still be glad to show {OTHER_objective}.

cheerful.li: No apprentice, so I'll write it all down instead for someone to find!

cold.li: What I know about {SUBJECT} stays with me, and that's the colony's loss more than mine.

warm.li: If there's a spare evening, I'd still love that chair, and so would my back.

blunt.li: Still on the stool, and my back's still sore.

gloomy.li: My back gets worse on that stool every day, and it's not much I'm asking.

warm.li: Never mind. Someone found me a cushion for the stool, which was kind of them.

cheerful.li: No soft chair, so I've folded my blanket into a cushion, and it's nearly as good!

warm.li: It fits as if it were made for me, thank you.

cheerful.li: Look at me! I clank when I walk, and I love it.

gloomy.li: It won't stop everything, but it might stop the one that matters.

cold.li: Good armor. My odds just improved.

blunt.li: No armor. Next raid, I'm standing at the back.

gloomy.li: Without armor I'm just meat on the wall, so remember that when you bury me.

cold.li: No armor. I'll take fewer risks, and the colony will get less from me in a fight.

blunt.li: Still no banner, so raise one.

cheerful.li: I've got the colors picked, and all I need now is cloth and a pole!

gloomy.li: Not a scrap of color over the gate, same as the day we came.

warm.li: No banner, but people still know this is home, and that will do.

cheerful.li: No banner? I'll hang my brightest shirt over the gate instead!

warm.li: I'd still love that bath whenever there's time, and I'll heat the water myself.

cheerful.li: I've been practicing my soaking, in case the bath ever comes!

gloomy.li: Another cold wash out of a bucket.

warm.li: I worry for whoever goes out next, with {OTHER_nameDef} still out there.

blunt.li: Why is {OTHER_nameDef} still alive?

cold.li: Every day {OTHER_nameDef} lives, it learns more of our habits.

warm.li: Please, everyone, go out in pairs while {OTHER_nameDef} is still around.

cheerful.li: Well, {OTHER_nameDef} got away, so I'm carrying a big stick everywhere now!

cold.li: When {OTHER_nameDef} comes back, I'll be the one who deals with it.

warm.li: I'd look after the bees myself, every day, if we had a hive for them.

blunt.li: The bees won't wait forever, so where's my hive?

gloomy.li: The wild bees will be gone before we get round to it.

warm.li: The wild bees found a hollow tree in the end, and I hope they do well there.

gloomy.li: No hive. The wild bees moved on, like everything does.

warm.li: No rush, but the years aren't waiting either.

blunt.li: I'm not getting younger while you think about it.

gloomy.li: Another birthday's coming, and still no pod.

warm.li: I'll grow old among friends, then, and there are worse ways.

cheerful.li: No pod, so I'll just be the most cheerful old wreck in the colony!

warm.li: If someone showed me how, I'd build the shelf myself and get the books off the floor.

blunt.li: Books on the floor and no shelf, and you can see the problem.

cold.li: Another book damaged today, which a shelf would have prevented.

warm.li: If a trader comes with books, I'd be so grateful for even one.

blunt.li: Still no new books, and I've memorized the old ones.

gloomy.li: I'm reading the same pages again, and they haven't improved.

blunt.li: The camp's still there and so am I, so let me go.

cheerful.li: I could hear them singing over at the camp, and I want to join in before they go!

gloomy.li: The {SUBJECT} will pack up soon, and I'll have missed it.

warm.li: I hope the {SUBJECT} had a good time here, even without me at their fire.

cheerful.li: Missed the camp, so I'll make my own fire and sing badly at it!

warm.li: I've been extra good, so can I have my lesson with {OTHER_nameDef} now?

blunt.li: Lesson. When?

gloomy.li: No one's said anything about my lesson, so I think they forgot.

warm.li: That's all right, {OTHER_nameDef} is busy, maybe when I'm bigger.

cheerful.li: I'm going to teach myself {SUBJECT}, and it can't be that hard!

warm.li: I left some food out for the {SUBJECT}, so can we catch it now?

cheerful.li: I just know the {SUBJECT} wants to live here with us!

gloomy.li: The {SUBJECT} will go away if nobody catches it soon.

warm.li: I hope the {SUBJECT} found a nice home somewhere else.

cheerful.li: The {SUBJECT} ran off, but I'm going to make friends with a beetle instead!

warm.li: There must be people out there wanting to hear from us too.

blunt.li: Still no comms console, and still no word from anyone.

cold.li: Every day without comms is a day of trade and help we can't call on.

warm.li: Maybe one day we'll hear from the others out there, and I hope they're well.

cheerful.li: No console! I'll just shout really loudly from the roof.

warm.li: A cool room would help the young and the old most of all, in this heat.

blunt.li: Still hot. Still no cool room.

gloomy.li: Another day like an oven, and I can barely think.

warm.li: I've been soaking cloths in water for whoever's flagging, which is something.

cheerful.li: No cool room, so I'll lie in the shade and pretend there's a breeze!

blunt.li: Crib, please, before the baby outgrows the crate.

cheerful.li: The little one's getting bigger every day, and the crate isn't!

gloomy.li: I watch the baby sleep in that crate and worry every night.

warm.li: I'd still like to see what's down there, and I'd run the drill myself.

blunt.li: The ore's down there and the drill isn't, so fix that.

cheerful.li: Steel, silver, maybe treasure, all of it right under our feet!

warm.li: Maybe another season, since the ore isn't going anywhere.

cheerful.li: The treasure stays buried, and it'll keep!

warm.li: I don't want to make a fuss, but I'm still hoping for something fine to wear.

cheerful.li: I've already decided where I'd wear it first, which is supper, obviously!

gloomy.li: Another patch on the elbow today, and something fine still feels a long way off.

warm.li: I'll chop if someone else hauls, so long as we get more wood in before the cold.

cheerful.li: Woodpile check: still small, so let's make it big!

gloomy.li: Every night we burn more wood than we cut.

warm.li: I'd still love a fishing spot, and I'd bring back enough for everyone.

blunt.li: Still no fishing spot.

gloomy.li: Stew again tonight, while the fish swim by.

warm.li: The water will still be there next season, I suppose.

cheerful.li: No fishing spot, so I'll catch them with my hands!

blunt.li: Still dirt under my bed.

cheerful.li: I've already picked out the boards I want for my floor!

gloomy.li: It rained again, and my room's mud again.

warm.li: I've laid a rug over the worst of the dirt, and it's homely, in its way.

cheerful.li: Dirt floor forever, and I'll call it rustic!

warm.li: Just a few flowers, whenever someone has a moment, to cheer the place up.

blunt.li: This place still looks like a quarry, so plant some flowers.

gloomy.li: The beds by the door are still bare, and I expect they'll stay that way.

warm.li: I found one wildflower by the wall and left it be, so that will have to do.

cheerful.li: No flowers? I'll paint some on the door instead!

warm.li: I'd feel so much better with something put by for the lean days.

blunt.li: Still nothing put by.

gloomy.li: Every day without a reserve is a day closer to a hungry one.

warm.li: We'll share what we have if it comes to it, as we always have.

cheerful.li: No reserve! I'll just have to eat very slowly this winter.

warm.li: Whenever there's stone to spare, I'd still love that fountain.

cheerful.li: I've already picked the spot in the yard where the fountain would go!

gloomy.li: I knew the fountain was a long shot, and it still is.

warm.li: It would have been lovely, the fountain, maybe one day.

cheerful.li: No fountain! I'll splash a bucket about and call it one.

warm.li: Even a few berries would do us good, before we all start looking pale.

blunt.li: Still eating meat, and still needing greens.

gloomy.li: My teeth ache, and still nothing fresh.

warm.li: I'll keep an eye out for wild berries past the fields.

cheerful.li: More meat! I'll pretend it's a vegetable.

warm.li: A bench outside would be lovely, whenever there's wood to spare.

blunt.li: Still sitting on the rock.

cheerful.li: Me, a bench and a sunset, that's all I'm dreaming of!

warm.li: I'll share the rock with whoever wants to sit a while.

gloomy.li: Back to the rock, and the rock is still hard.

warm.li: Summer won't last, and a grill would give us a few good evenings together.

blunt.li: Grill, while it's still summer.

cheerful.li: Any news on the grill, because I can almost smell it already!

warm.li: We'll have our grilled supper next summer, I'm sure of it.

cheerful.li: No grill! I'll hold a skewer over the stove and call it the same thing.

warm.li: I'd love the next visitors to have somewhere proper to sleep.

blunt.li: Guests still sleeping on the floor.

cold.li: Visitors remember how they're treated, and right now they remember the floor.

warm.li: I'll give up my bed to the next guest myself, if it comes to that.

cheerful.li: No guest bed, so I'll lend them my best blanket instead!

warm.li: I'd still love the guest room fixed up, for our visitors' sake.

blunt.li: The guest room's still bad, so fix it.

gloomy.li: Another guest, another apology for the room.

warm.li: I'll put a flower in the guest room myself, as a start.

cheerful.li: The guest room stays rough, and we'll call it charming!

warm.li: Still hoping for a hat, if anyone has a moment at the tailor's bench.

blunt.li: My head's still bare.

gloomy.li: The sun's still burning my scalp.

warm.li: A cloth tied round my head does the job, more or less.

gloomy.li: No hat. My head and the weather will just have to fight it out.

blunt.li: We're short of fodder for winter, so fix it.

cheerful.li: The animals and I are still hoping for a full barn!

gloomy.li: The grass is going brown, and the barn's still half empty.

warm.li: I'd feel better with a few rows of healroot in, and I'll tend them myself.

blunt.li: No healroot. Still.

gloomy.li: Fever season's coming, and we've nothing to meet it with.

warm.li: We'll look after each other as best we can, herbs or no herbs.

cheerful.li: No healroot! I'll just have to stay very healthy.

warm.li: I'd still be so grateful for a fire in my room, when there's time.

cheerful.li: I've been imagining a fire in my room every night, and it's a warm thought at least!

gloomy.li: Still cold in my room, and still waiting.

warm.li: A bit more honey would sweeten everyone's day, and I'd share mine round.

blunt.li: The honey jar's empty, so someone fill it.

gloomy.li: Plain bread again, and no honey for it.

warm.li: The old ones' hands go white in the cold wash, so hot water would help them most.

blunt.li: Water. Still cold.

gloomy.li: My teeth were chattering through the whole wash again.

warm.li: I'll warm a pot on the stove for whoever needs it, slow as that is.

cheerful.li: Cold water it is, and very bracing it'll be!

gloomy.li: Cold water forever, then, and cold hands with it.

warm.li: The cooks are still making do, so let me bring them something fresh.

gloomy.li: The deer are fat and we're eating porridge.

cold.li: The herd is still in range, though every day we wait it moves further off.

blunt.li: Good, {OTHER_nameDef}'s patched up.

cheerful.li: {OTHER_nameDef} is back on {OTHER_possessive} feet and eating again, thank you!

cold.li: {OTHER_nameDef} will recover, so the training wasn't wasted.

warm.li: No one came, so I did what I could for {OTHER_nameDef} and hoped it was enough.

blunt.li: No doctor came, so I bandaged {OTHER_nameDef} myself.

gloomy.li: {OTHER_nameDef} waited, and no one came, and I'll remember that.

cold.li: If {OTHER_nameDef} dies of this, it was a choice the council made.

warm.li: I'm still hoping for more medicine, to be ready for whoever's next.

cheerful.li: The medicine shelf is very tidy, because it's very empty!

gloomy.li: I checked the medicine shelf again, and nothing's grown back on it.

warm.li: I know it's a small, silly thing to want, but I'd treasure it.

cheerful.li: A ring, a pin, anything shiny at all would make my day!

gloomy.li: Still nothing pretty, not that I really expected it.

warm.li: There are more important things than jewelry, and I'll be fine.

blunt.li: No jewelry, fine, didn't need it.
Still waiting on those lessons from {OTHER_nameDef}.

cheerful.li: Any day now, I'm ready to learn from {OTHER_nameDef}!

gloomy.li: Still teaching myself {SUBJECT}, badly.

warm.li: Maybe {OTHER_nameDef} will have time another day, and I'll keep practicing.

cheerful.li: I'll watch {OTHER_nameDef} from the corner and learn by spying!

warm.li: It would do us all good to sit down together for a meeting, when there's an evening free.

cheerful.li: I've got a list of ideas for the next meeting, and they're all brilliant!

gloomy.li: Things keep getting decided without us, and still no meeting.

warm.li: I'll say what I wanted to say over supper, then, gently.

cheerful.li: No meeting! I'll hold my own and invite the chickens.

warm.li: A sculpture would brighten the place, and I'd help carry the stone.

blunt.li: Still ugly in here, and still no sculpture.

gloomy.li: Blank walls again today.

warm.li: Perhaps someone will carve something in their free time, and I'd love that.

cheerful.li: No sculpture, so I'll stack some pretty rocks and call it art!

warm.li: Music again, in this place, and thank you for it.

blunt.li: Good, and now no more whistling.

gloomy.li: A sad song, finally, and it suits us.

cold.li: The instrument is adequate, and morale will follow.

plain.li: The evenings are as quiet as ever, without music.

warm.li: I'll hum for anyone who wants a tune, though it's not the same.

blunt.li: No music. Just silence and whistling.

cheerful.li: No instrument, so I'll drum on the table instead!

gloomy.li: No music. The quiet's the only tune we get.

cold.li: The council has chosen silence, and morale will show it.

warm.li: Even a small chest of silver put by would help us all sleep easier.

cheerful.li: The treasury is still a drawer, but a drawer with dreams!

gloomy.li: Nothing saved, so one bad season and we're done.

warm.li: If there's any outdoor work going, I'd still love it.

blunt.li: Still inside. Still want out.

cold.li: My work is slipping, and the walls are the cause. I'm still asking to go outside.

warm.li: One evening together would do everyone so much good. I'd cook for it, if that helps.

blunt.li: Party. People are snapping. Soon.

cold.li: Morale hasn't improved. A party would still be the cheapest fix.

blunt.li: Build the circle before I set the table on fire.

cheerful.li: I've drawn the circle in chalk on the floor! It's not the same, though.

gloomy.li: Still working magic between the bread and the salt.

warm.li: I'll keep my workings small and quiet, so I don't frighten anyone.

cheerful.li: No circle! I'll practice in the field and hope the sparks miss the hay.

blunt.li: The {SUBJECT}. Still out there. Let me go.

cheerful.li: The {SUBJECT} is still hanging about! I think it likes us.

gloomy.li: The {SUBJECT} will be gone any day now.

warm.li: I hope the {SUBJECT} is happy out there, wherever it went.

cheerful.li: The {SUBJECT} got away, but there'll be another one!

warm.li: The animals would be safer in a pen, and the crops too. I'd mend the fences myself.

blunt.li: Animals in the crops again. Pen.

gloomy.li: Another day chasing animals out of the fields.

warm.li: I'll keep an eye on the animals myself, then.

cheerful.li: No pen? Then I'll get very fast at chasing!

blunt.li: {OTHER_nameDef}'s bed's in. Good.

gloomy.li: {OTHER_nameDef} sleeps by me now. It's the best I've slept in a while.

cold.li: {OTHER_nameDef} sleeps in my room now. We'll both rest better.

warm.li: I put a blanket out for {OTHER_nameDef} by the pen. It's the best I could do.

blunt.li: No bed. {OTHER_nameDef} sleeps outside, I guess.

gloomy.li: {OTHER_nameDef} sleeps out in the cold, and I lie awake listening for {OTHER_objective}.

cold.li: {OTHER_nameDef} sleeps with the herd. My handling will suffer for it.

warm.li: I'd like it ready before I need it, so nobody has to rush when the time comes.

blunt.li: Still no resting place. I'm not getting younger.

cold.li: My resting place remains unbuilt. Time is not on my side.

warm.li: Wherever you put me, put me near the others. That's what matters.

cheerful.li: No sarcophagus! I'll just have to keep living, then.

warm.li: A sauna would warm all of us through. I'd keep the stones hot for everyone.

blunt.li: Cold. No sauna. Still.

gloomy.li: Another frozen day. Still no sauna.

warm.li: I'll warm some stones in the fire and sit by them. It's a start.

cheerful.li: No sauna? I'll sit very close to the stove and sweat anyway!

warm.li: I'd still make the scarecrow myself, if someone could spare the wood.

blunt.li: Something's eating the crops. Still.

gloomy.li: More of the field gone last night.

warm.li: I'll walk the rows at dawn myself and shoo them off.

cheerful.li: No scarecrow? I'll stand out there and wave my arms!

blunt.li: Still eating standing up.

cheerful.li: One day we'll all fit at the table! I'm saving a seat for that day.

gloomy.li: Ate standing by the door again.

warm.li: I'll take my bowl outside and leave the chair for someone else.

cheerful.li: No more chairs! I'll eat sitting on the woodpile, like a king on a throne.

blunt.li: Still praying behind the storeroom. Still smells.

cheerful.li: I've found the perfect spot for a shrine! It's just waiting.

gloomy.li: Still no shrine. The prayers smell of rot.

warm.li: I'll pray where I can. I'm sure I'm still heard.

cheerful.li: No shrine! I'll pray under the open sky, which is the biggest shrine there is.

blunt.li: Still sick. Still no sickbed.

cheerful.li: Still coughing, still hoping! A sickbed would be lovely.

gloomy.li: I'm getting worse, and there's still nowhere for the sick.

warm.li: I'm better now. I hope whoever's ill next has somewhere to lie.

cheerful.li: I got better anyway! Coughing in the barracks builds character.

warm.li: {OTHER_nameDef} must be busy. I'll be glad to see {OTHER_objective} when I'm up.

cheerful.li: No visit, but I counted every crack in the ceiling. There are forty!

gloomy.li: I waited for {OTHER_nameDef} all week. Nobody comes in here.

cold.li: {OTHER_nameDef} didn't come. I've noted it.

warm.li: I hate seeing good meat wasted. A smokehouse would save so much.

blunt.li: More rotten meat. Build the smokehouse.

gloomy.li: The flies ate better than we did this week.

warm.li: I'll salt what I can by hand. It's slow, but it helps.

cheerful.li: No smokehouse! I'll just eat faster.

warm.li: I'd cut the blocks myself if someone could spare me from other work.

blunt.li: Blocks. None cut. Still.

gloomy.li: Still building with wood that'll burn.

warm.li: We'll build with what we've got. It'll hold, I hope.

cheerful.li: No blocks! Wood is lovely too, as long as nobody brings a torch.

warm.li: I'd share any new book with the others, I promise.

cheerful.li: Any new books yet? I've finished the old ones again!

gloomy.li: Same books again. I know all the endings.

warm.li: That's all right. I'll ask someone to tell me a story instead.

cheerful.li: No new books! I'll write my own, with dragons.

warm.li: A cup of tea would help so much, and I'd share the pot with the others who are coughing.

blunt.li: Tea. Still none. Still coughing.

gloomy.li: Still sick. Still no tea.

warm.li: I'm getting better anyway. Thank you all for the blankets.

cheerful.li: No tea! Hot water with a leaf in it is nearly the same.

warm.li: The sky's beautiful tonight. A telescope would let everyone see it closer.

cheerful.li: Clear skies again! Perfect telescope weather, if we had one.

gloomy.li: Another clear night wasted, squinting.

warm.li: I'll still show anyone who asks the stars I know, telescope or not.

cheerful.li: No telescope! I'll stand on the roof and get a bit closer.

warm.li: The whole place is clean. Thank you, everyone who scrubbed.

blunt.li: Clean. Keep it that way.

cheerful.li: Everything's sparkling! I could eat off the floor, and I might.

gloomy.li: Clean, for now. Enjoy it while it lasts.

warm.li: I'll clean a corner every day myself. It's a start.

blunt.li: Still filthy. I'm done asking.

cheerful.li: The mess wins this round! I'll start on my corner tomorrow.

gloomy.li: The dirt's here to stay, like the rest of us.

cold.li: The filth remains. The sickness it brings will be the council's responsibility.

warm.li: I know it's not glamorous, but {THING} would help us all.

cheerful.li: Still going outside! I've got to know the bushes very well.

gloomy.li: Another cold morning behind the woodpile.

warm.li: I'll dig a proper pit, at least, away from the water.

cheerful.li: No toilet? The bushes and I will stay close friends!

warm.li: A tool cabinet would help everyone at the bench, not just me. I'd sort the tools into it myself.

blunt.li: Lost the chisel again.

cheerful.li: I've drawn where every tool would hang! I just need the cabinet.

warm.li: I'll put pegs on the wall for the tools for now. It helps.

cheerful.li: No cabinet! I'll just carry all the tools in my pockets.

warm.li: I'd take good care of that {THINGBARE}, if there's any chance.

cheerful.li: The {THINGBARE} is still in {OTHER_nameDef}'s pack! It's waiting for me.

gloomy.li: {OTHER_nameDef} will pack up soon, and the {THINGBARE} will go too.

warm.li: I'd train the others too, if we had somewhere to practice.

cheerful.li: Still punching fence posts! The fence posts are losing.

gloomy.li: I'm getting slower every day, and the next raid won't wait.

warm.li: If a caravan goes out, I'd love to go along and help.

blunt.li: Caravan. Me on it. When?

gloomy.li: Same hills out the window again today. I've stopped looking at them.

warm.li: Something warm to wear would see me through the cold. I'd mend it myself whenever it tears.

blunt.li: Still cold. Still no coat.

cheerful.li: I've been wearing my blanket as a cape! It's not ideal.

warm.li: Somewhere to wash would make everyone's day better. I'd fill the tub for whoever goes first.

blunt.li: Still nowhere to wash.

gloomy.li: I smell worse every day.

warm.li: I'll fetch a bucket from the river and share it round.

blunt.li: No wash place. Everyone stinks. Fine.

cheerful.li: No tub! I'll wait for the next rain and dance in it.

warm.li: A rack would help us all get to the wall quicker. I'd keep it tidy, every piece in its place.

blunt.li: Weapons on the floor. Still.

gloomy.li: The next raid will find our weapons under someone's bed again.

warm.li: I'll lay everyone's gear out by the door myself, at least.

cheerful.li: No rack! I'll hang everything on the coat pegs.
